He was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 1999. A native of [[Cleveland]], Ohio, Mack played [[college football]] as an [[End (gridiron football)|end]] and [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|tackle]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] from 1963 to 1965. Mack was selected by the Rams with the [[List of second overall NFL draft picks|second overall pick]] of the [[1966 NFL draft]] and played at [[Guard (gridiron football)|left guard]] for the Rams for 13 seasons from 1966 to 1978. During his NFL career, Mack played in 11 [[Pro Bowl]]s and appeared in 184 consecutive games, 176 as a starter, over 13 seasons.

'''Thomas Louie Jackson''', also referred to as "'''TJ'''" or "'''Tommy'''", (born April 4, 1951) is an American [[sports commentator]] and former professional [[American football|football]] player. He played as a [[linebacker]] for the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1973 to 1986. He was a member of Denver's "[[Orange Crush Defense]]" and helped lead the Broncos to the AFC Championship in [[1977–78 NFL playoffs#AFC: Denver Broncos 20, Oakland Raiders 17|1977]] and [[1986–87 NFL playoffs#AFC: Denver Broncos 23, Cleveland Browns 20 (OT)|1986]] . After his playing career ended, he enjoyed a successful 29-year run as an NFL analyst for [[ESPN]]. He was given the [[Pete Rozelle Award]] for excellence in broadcasting by the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2015.

Newberry''' (born December 20, 1962) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] for 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). '''Thomas Arthur Keating''' (September 2, 1942 – August 31, 2012) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] from 1961 to 1963 and played 12 seasons in the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1964 to 1975. He was an [[American Football League All-Star game|AFL All-Star]] in 1966 and 1967, a key to the [[1967 Oakland Raiders season|1967 Oakland Raiders]]' defensive line that led the team to a 13–1 record and the [[1967 American Football League Championship Game|1967 AFL Championship]], and was considered "''the premier tackle in the old American Football League''".<ref name=Time/>  He was known for his use of a distinctive four-point stance in which he lined up with both hands on the ground.<ref name=SF>{{cite news|author=Vic Tafur|title=Ex-Raiders lineman Tom Keating dies|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=September 4, 2012|url=http://www.sfgate.com/raiders/article/Ex-Raiders-lineman-Tom-Keating-dies-3839971.php}}</ref>

[[tight end]] from [[Bucknell University]] and member of the Bucknell Athletics Hall of Fame, Mitchell played one season ([[1966 Oakland Raiders season|1966]]) for the [[American Football League]] (AFL)'s [[Oakland Raiders]], and ten seasons ([[1968 NFL season|1968]]–[[1977 NFL season|1977]]) in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Baltimore Colts]] and the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He was nicknamed "'''the Crocodile'''" and his pouring of a pitcher of beer on the head of author [[George Plimpton]] is recounted in the book ''Mad Ducks and Bears''.
